cc.title: Peak heating rate (2-s window)
cc.idea: How fast the Peltier elements can heat the block: the steepest 2-second slope of every heating transition, median over the run (manual: 4.8 °C/s). Independent of plateau detection, so short holds do not distort it.
cc.reading: A slow fall over months is Peltier or thermal-interface ageing; the fitted line gives a conditional limit-crossing estimate, not a failure date. A single low run points to the plate or a blocked vent that day.
cc.source: LC TemperatureLog · QS log sample temperature

cc.title: Peak cooling rate (2-s window)
cc.idea: How well the heat sink and fans remove heat: steepest 2-second cooling slope of every transition, median over the run (manual: 2.5 °C/s).
cc.reading: Falling cooling with stable heating = clogged fan filter or failing fan (clean the filters, check fans) before Peltier replacement.

cc.title: Overshoot at the denaturation step
cc.idea: Block temperature beyond the setpoint before it settles. The LC480 overshoots 4–6 °C by design, identically every cycle.
cc.reading: Watch for change, not size: a CUSUM drifting up or down means the controller or the temperature sensor has changed.

cc.title: Settling time at the denaturation step
cc.idea: Seconds from the 90 % point until the block stays within ±0.5 °C of the setpoint.
cc.reading: Longer settling with a normal ramp rate points to control tuning or sensor lag.

cc.title: Transition time A → B °C
cc.idea: Seconds the block needs to go from one programmed temperature to the next (e.g. 95 → 60 °C): from leaving ±0.5 °C of the start temperature until first within ±0.5 °C of the target, median over all cycles of the run. One chart per transition of the program. Includes ramp and overshoot, so it shows how much of every cycle is spent moving instead of holding.
cc.reading: Compare a transition only with itself and the same program. A cooling transition that lengthens while heating transitions stay flat points to heat removal (fans, filters, heat sink); all transitions lengthening together points to the Peltier elements or the room.
cc.source: LC TemperatureLog · QS log sample temperature · run program

cc.title: Temperature at the moment of reading
cc.idea: Offset (X̄) and stability (S) of the block while the camera reads, one subgroup per run.
cc.reading: X̄ drifting away from its usual offset = temperature calibration drift (verify with a temperature plate). S rising = unstable control.
cc.source: LC temperature of every acquisition · QS sample temperature of every image

cc.title: Block zone uniformity (95th percentile)
cc.idea: Difference between the warmest and coolest of the six zones, 95th percentile over the run.
cc.reading: An EWMA creeping up means one zone is losing its match; look at the Temperature graph to find which.

cc.title: Heat-sink maximum
cc.idea: Highest heat-sink temperature during the run.
cc.reading: Rising over time with the same protocol = cooling capacity dropping (fans, dust, room temperature).

cc.title: Heated cover temperature
cc.idea: Median cover temperature during the run (setpoint 105 °C).
cc.reading: Below the setpoint = cover heater fault; condensation and evaporation follow.

cc.title: Lamp reference channel (stability)
cc.idea: The instrument measures the Xenon lamp through a reference channel and compensates for it. In 155 runs from 2022–2026 the value stayed within ±1 %, so it shows regulation, not lamp ageing. Lamp hours and intensity % are only in Tools → Instruments (manual p. 208).
cc.reading: Stable = the lamp is still inside the range the instrument can compensate. A step or a point outside the limits = lamp, light guide or reference-sensor fault; check the lamp intensity % in the instrument software.
cc.source: LC AcquisitionStore RefValue, first reading of the run, per filter pair

cc.title: Lamp drift within a run
cc.idea: How much the lamp intensity changes during one run.
cc.reading: Growing drift is typical of a lamp near the end of its life.
cc.source: LC RefValue first vs last reading

cc.title: LED drive current
cc.idea: Median LED current during the run.
cc.reading: The instrument raises current to keep light output: a rising trend is LED ageing; the line predicts when it reaches the limit you set.

cc.title: LED junction temperature (maximum)
cc.idea: Hottest LED junction temperature in the run.
cc.reading: Higher than usual = LED cooling problem; LEDs age faster when hot.

cc.title: Automatic integration time / exposure
cc.idea: Both instruments lengthen exposure automatically when the signal is weak.
cc.reading: A slow rise is compatible with weaker signal; verify matched controls and optical configuration before attributing ageing (compare with B-H8/B-H10); a jump after a reagent change points to the method instead.
cc.source: LC IntgrTime per channel · QS exposure per filter

cc.title: Saturated well images
cc.idea: Share of well images with at least one saturated pixel.
cc.reading: A rise = exposure logic or camera fault, or overloaded samples; values above zero make the curve plateau unreliable.

cc.title: Uniformity calibration: edge-to-centre ratio
cc.idea: Changes only when the instrument is recalibrated.
cc.reading: A step at a recalibration shows how much the optics changed; a large step deserves a service question.

cc.title: Background calibration: mean offset
cc.idea: Mean absolute background offset of the last background calibration.
cc.reading: Rising between calibrations = contamination of the block or optics.

cc.title: Well-position (ROI) calibration: spot diameter
cc.idea: Mean spot diameter from the ROI calibration.
cc.reading: A change means the optical alignment moved.

cc.title: Filter-wheel move time
cc.idea: Median time of a filter-wheel move.
cc.reading: Slower moves = motor or bearing wear.

cc.title: Filter-wheel moves slower than 500 ms
cc.idea: Share of moves longer than 500 ms (normal ≈ 300 ms).
cc.reading: Occasional stalls come before a failure; any upward trend is worth a service call.

cc.title: Filter-wheel position offset
cc.idea: Encoder offset after each move; constant for a healthy wheel.
cc.reading: Any step = the wheel slipped, was re-homed or serviced.

cc.title: Camera readout time beyond the exposure
cc.idea: About 0.5 s per image; one subgroup = all images of the run.
cc.reading: A jump = camera or its interface; a slow rise = controller slowing (compare with software charts).
cc.source: QS log CAMera start/end minus requested exposure

cc.title: Channel switch time
cc.idea: Time between the channels of one reading, net of integration (≈ 1.0–1.4 s; filter switch < 0.65 s by the manual).
cc.reading: Rising = filter wheels or camera readout slowing.
cc.source: LC acquisition times minus integration time

cc.title: Heated cover lowering time
cc.idea: Motorised cover pressing onto the plate (≈ 10 s).
cc.reading: Getting slower = motor or linkage wear, or plates/seals that are too tall.

cc.title: Heated cover raising time
cc.idea: Cover lifting off the plate (≈ 5.4 s).
cc.reading: As B-H18.

cc.title: Background fluorescence per channel
cc.idea: Median background of all wells, per channel.
cc.reading: Slow decline = light source ageing; a raised run = plate, seal or contamination.

cc.title: End-point fluorescence per channel
cc.idea: Median end-point of all wells, per channel.
cc.reading: Moves together with B-H8/B-H10 when optics age; alone it points to the method (probe) — see M-group.

cc.title: Run duration
cc.idea: Only comparable between runs of the same protocol.
cc.reading: A much shorter or longer run with the same protocol = aborted, paused or held run.

cc.title: Reply time to the PC software
cc.idea: How fast the embedded computer answers commands.
cc.reading: Rising = controller overloaded or network problem.

cc.title: Once-per-second timer lateness
cc.idea: How late the 1-s housekeeping timer fires.
cc.reading: Rising = the embedded CPU is saturated (mostly while imaging).

cc.title: Scheduler falling behind
cc.idea: How often the task scheduler had to catch up, per hour of run.
cc.reading: A u-chart above its limit = the internal computer is overloaded.

cc.title: Image → processing delay
cc.idea: Time from the last image to the start of its processing.
cc.reading: Rising = storage or CPU slowing; one long delay is a single stall.

cc.title: Image analysis time
cc.idea: The software's own processing time per image.
cc.reading: A step after an update = different firmware behaviour (see version markers).

cc.title: Run-time prediction error
cc.idea: Actual minus predicted run time.
cc.reading: Creeping up = actions take longer than the firmware expects.

cc.title: Data hand-off time
cc.idea: Minutes from run end until the data were packed for the PC.
cc.reading: Long = network or PC problem, or a manual delay.

cc.title: Command errors in the instrument log
cc.idea: Count of command errors per run.
cc.reading: New or more errors = firmware or configuration change.

cc.title: Cycle-timing regularity
cc.idea: Standard deviation of the cycle period within a run.
cc.reading: Larger = scheduling problems in the instrument.
cc.source: LC acquisition times · QS image times

cc.title: Temperature-log intervals over 500 ms
cc.idea: Regularity of the control-loop logging.
cc.reading: Any rise = controller overload.

cc.title: Invalid fluorescence readings
cc.idea: Readings the instrument marked invalid.
cc.reading: Above zero = acquisition fault.

cc.title: Stored Ct not reproducible (> 0.2)
cc.idea: Wells whose stored Ct differs from the recalculation.
cc.reading: Non-zero requires checking algorithm, precision, stored settings and provenance; it does not establish post-analysis editing.

cc.title: Run end → last change
cc.idea: Processing delay on a log scale (0 = 1 h, 1 = 10 h, 2 = 100 h).
cc.reading: Points above the limit are late edits; cross-check with the operator group.

cc.title: Forensic findings per run
cc.idea: Count of review and error findings for the run.
cc.reading: A run above the limit needs a closer look in the forensic log.

cc.title: Positive control Cq (Levey-Jennings)
cc.idea: Mean Cq of the positive control per run and target, with Westgard rules.
cc.reading: Across-run rules flag unexpected control behaviour. R-4s is not applied to run means. Investigate lot, extraction batch, assay and instrument effects.

cc.title: Probe signal strength (positive control)
cc.idea: Amplitude (plateau above background) of the same control each run.
cc.reading: Falling with a stable Cq = probe or dye degradation (storage, freeze-thaw); a step at a lot change = the lot. Compare with B-H8/B-H10 to exclude the optics.
cc.source: stored curves of the positive control

cc.title: Passive reference (ROX) level
cc.idea: Median passive-reference level of named wells.
cc.reading: A step = new master-mix lot or ROX concentration.

cc.title: PCR efficiency from the standards
cc.idea: Efficiency of the standard curve per run and target.
cc.reading: A slow drop = degrading standard or reagent; outside 90–110 % fails MIQE-style acceptance.

cc.title: Negative controls by process stage
cc.idea: Share of negative-control wells with any Cq.
cc.reading: Rising = contamination of reagents or of the working area (ISFG, MIQE).

cc.title: IC shift from fixed reference
cc.idea: Mean IC Cq shift from the configured fixed reference. Missing reference means unavailable; endogenous taxon targets are not fixed-input IPCs.
cc.reading: Upward drift = extraction method or kit problem.

cc.title: Low Cq confidence
cc.idea: Share of wells flagged for low Cq confidence.
cc.reading: A rise = noisy curves, often probe or baseline problems.

cc.title: Late signal / stochastic-zone results
cc.idea: Share of sample results falling in the late-signal or low-quantity zone.
cc.reading: A rise = sensitivity drop or poorer samples.

cc.title: Replicate precision (pooled SD, Cq < 30)
cc.idea: Pipetting precision; replicates above Cq 30 are left out so stochastic noise does not hide skill.
cc.reading: One operator's points above the others → retraining; everyone rising → pipette calibration.

cc.title: Dispensed-volume spread (ROX CV)
cc.idea: Raw passive-reference level varies with the dispensed volume.
cc.reading: High CV = uneven pipetting or bubbles.

cc.title: Row / column pattern
cc.idea: Largest mean Cq offset of a plate row or column.
cc.reading: One row or column off = a faulty multichannel tip or loading-order error.
cc.source: replicate residuals by plate row and column

cc.title: Contamination rate by operator (funnel)
cc.idea: NTC positives per operator against the number of NTCs they ran.
cc.reading: Outside the 99.8 % line → investigate; the funnel keeps small workloads from looking unfair.

cc.title: Repeat / inconclusive / invalid rate by operator (funnel)
cc.idea: Analytical robustness per person.
cc.reading: As B-O5.

cc.title: Manual interventions
cc.idea: Share of settings or wells changed by hand.
cc.reading: High or rising → ask for documented reasons (OIG report lessons); compare operators with the funnel view.
cc.source: manual threshold/baseline, omitted wells, manual calls

cc.title: Stored calls that disagree with the SOP
cc.idea: Consistency and fairness: do calls follow the written rules?
cc.reading: Disagreement concentrated in one person or case type → training or bias check.

cc.title: Copied-data events
cc.idea: Must be zero.
cc.reading: Any event is a forensic finding.

graphs.title: Run timeline — created, run, analysis, last change
graphs.note: Every dated event the file carries: experiment creation, run start and end, analysis creation and edits, the last recorded change (for .eds, the newest ZIP entry date is the last save), instrument log and calibrations. Events more than 7 days from the run are listed in the table and marked at the edge.

graphs.title: Amplification curves coloured by SOP outcome
graphs.note: Stored curves of the selected target. Colour = outcome under the active SOP; dashed vertical lines = SOP Cq cut-off and late-signal limit; horizontal line = stored threshold (QuantStudio ΔRn).

graphs.title: Plate heat map
graphs.note: Every physical position. Choose what the colour shows: SOP outcome, stored Cq, end fluorescence, background, amplitude, or analysis status (which also shows wells with signal that are in no analysis, and omitted wells).

graphs.title: Signal in wells that are not in any analysis
graphs.note: Rising fluorescence in positions that carry no result (unnamed wells, wells left out of every analysis, or wells without a target). These are the places where a sample may have been run but not reported.

graphs.title: Cq by target with SOP cut-offs
graphs.note: One point per well. Colour by SOP outcome or by role. Red dashed line: Cq cut-off; orange: late-signal limit (per target).

graphs.title: Replicate spread — mean Cq against SD
graphs.note: One point per sample and target with two or more detected replicates. The dashed line is the SOP maximum SD.

graphs.title: Standard curve with residuals and SOP limits
graphs.note: Cq against log10 of the stored standard quantity, fitted by least squares on this page. The label shows slope, R², efficiency and range against the SOP limits; residuals are in the table.

graphs.title: Internal control / reference Cq per sample (inhibition)
graphs.note: Cq of the targets the SOP marks as internal control or reference. The band is the run median ± the SOP maximum IC shift; points above it suggest inhibition or low input.

graphs.title: Fluorescence level against Cq
graphs.note: End-point fluorescence (or amplitude above background) against the stored Cq. Late, low-plateau curves separate from true amplification; undetected wells are drawn at the right edge.

graphs.title: Background and plateau fluorescence per channel
graphs.note: For each detection channel / target: background (mean of cycles 3–10) and end-point fluorescence of every well, including wells outside the analyses. A shifted background points to plate, seal or optical problems.

graphs.title: SOP outcomes per target
graphs.note: Number of sample/target results per outcome under the active SOP, controls included.

graphs.title: Block, cover and zone temperature (QuantStudio log)
graphs.note: From the instrument log inside the .eds file: sample block mean, heated cover and the spread between block zones, against minutes from the first record. The dashed line is the SOP maximum zone spread.

graphs.title: Stored Ct against the Ct re-derived on this page
graphs.note: QuantStudio only: difference between the stored Ct and the crossing of the stored ΔRn with the stored threshold. Differences beyond ±0.2 require an algorithm/settings/provenance review; they do not prove that stored data were edited.

graphs.title: Block temperature trace (LightCycler temperature log)
graphs.note: The block temperature the LightCycler 480 logged about every 0.41 s, decoded from the TemperatureLog inside the .ixo file, with the protocol setpoints. Heating and cooling rates, overshoot, settling and transition times on the control panel are measured on the full trace; the graph keeps the lowest and highest value of every time slice, so overshoots and short holds are not lost when it is thinned for display.

graphs.title: Runs on a calendar — run time and last change
graphs.note: Each run as a green dot at its start, with the experiment creation (blue, above) and the last recorded change (red, below, joined by a dashed line). Long gaps between run and last change are the first thing an auditor asks about.

graphs.title: Hours from run end to the last recorded change
graphs.note: Processing time per run. The dashed line is the SOP maximum; bars above it are flagged in the run acceptance.

graphs.title: Run acceptance grid
graphs.note: Runs (rows) against the SOP criteria (columns): green met, amber review, red rejected, grey not applicable.

graphs.title: SOP outcomes per run
graphs.note: Stacked counts of sample/target outcomes for every loaded run.

graphs.title: Control Cq across runs with SOP range
graphs.note: Descriptive control overview. Solid band: configured SOP range. No pooled statistical limits; use extraction-batch charts for comparable groups.

graphs.title: Background and plateau fluorescence across runs
graphs.note: Median background and median end-point fluorescence of every channel per run: slow drift here is an instrument or reagent trend.

graphs.title: Run duration and instrument use
graphs.note: Minutes from run start to run end, coloured by instrument. A run much shorter than its siblings with the same protocol deserves a look at the log.

graphs.title: Forensic findings by area (Pareto)
graphs.note: Count of error and review findings in the forensic log, grouped by area, largest first.

graphs.title: Control extraction batches
graphs.note: Descriptive association only. Separate material, extraction batch, dilution, target, instrument and protocol. Missing/invalid extraction dates are excluded from age plots.

graphs.title: Control extract age versus Cq
graphs.note: Descriptive association only. Separate material, extraction batch, dilution, target, instrument and protocol. Missing/invalid extraction dates are excluded from age plots.

graphs.title: Control Cq versus cooling rate
graphs.note: Descriptive association only. Separate material, extraction batch, dilution, target, instrument and protocol. Missing/invalid extraction dates are excluded from age plots.
